lines.text: You've got three commands on your mechanism, and nothing that runs them yet. This is where one of them gets a button.
You made this teleop file yourself in Project Setup. The annotation on the class is what puts it on the driver station, and without it there's nothing to choose.
So far it's one empty constructor, and this lesson fills it. Edit this file and don't make a new one, because a second teleop class means two teleops on the list.
The controller goes in the robot class, right beside the mechanisms. Put it there once, and every OpMode you ever write reaches it the same way.
It's two additions. The import goes up top, then the field, and the zero is the port the controller sits on at the driver station.
Now the teleop itself. Its whole contents get replaced, and what's left is short: one class, one constructor, one binding.
The constructor is handed the robot. That's how this file gets to your mechanism, and to the controller you just added.
Read the binding left to right. It picks the left trigger, and the first half runs the fast command for as long as the trigger's held, then cancels it when you let go.
The second half covers the release. Once the trigger comes up it runs a command of its own, and here that's stop.
A passing build isn't enough here, because nothing moves yet. Search the folder for the teleop annotation too, and make sure it turns up exactly once.
Every binding line gets a release. Why it needs one is something you'll see for yourself next, in Hardware Simulation, when you finally pull the trigger.
